summary: Payment failures (error rate ~60% from 15:00) are NOT caused by the payment-service v6.0.0 release. The true fault is in the shared ledger-db (Postgres): disk usage climbed steadily from 84% at 12:00 to 100% at ~15:02, driven by an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining tens of GB of WAL. When the disk filled, writes failed with 'No space left on device', breaking ledger writes for every tenant of ledger-db. The 14:46 deploy of v6.0.0 and the 15:12 rollback are temporally coincidental: errors began only when disk hit 100% (~15:00), the first slot warning (14:34) predates the deploy, co-tenant order-service failed identically without any deploy, and rolling back payment-service did NOT stop the errors (they continue through 16:57 with disk still 100%). Category: resource_exhaustion originating in ledger-db.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from inactive replication slot retaining WAL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: An inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' on the shared ledger-db retained tens of GB of WAL, filling the data volume to 100% around 15:02. With no free space, Postgres could not extend files or write WAL, so every ledger write from its tenants (payment-service, order-service, ...) failed with 'No space left on device'. payment-service's 60% error rate and the ledger write failures are downstream symptoms; v6.0.0 is a coincidental correlation.

causal_chain.claim: Inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' stops advancing, so Postgres retains all WAL
Retained WAL + normal data growth push ledger-db disk from 84% (12:00) to 100% (~15:02)
At 100% disk, Postgres cannot extend files/write WAL -> 'No space left on device'
All ledger-db tenants fail writes: payment-service and order-service both report identical errors
payment-service surfaces ~60% error rate; rollback of v6.0.0 cannot help because fault is in the DB

assumptions: The 84%-to-100% disk growth is attributable primarily to the retained WAL (slot warnings show 33-77 GB retained), not an unmeasured data load.
No other unobserved process independently filled the disk.

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 introduced a faulty ledger write / new MANDATE_HOLD entry type
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v6.0.0 release (new mandate flow + new MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type) caused the ledger write failures and 60% payment error rate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Error onset (~15:00) tracks the disk reaching 100%, not the 14:46 deploy (~15 min gap). The first WAL-retention warning (14:34) predates the deploy. Errors are 'No space left on device', not a MANDATE_HOLD/type error. Rolling back at 15:12 did NOT stop errors (295 continued through 16:57). Co-tenant order-service failed identically with no deploy of its own. This is a shared-infrastructure fault, not a code fault.

facts.statement: payment-service error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~61% at the 15:00 bucket and stayed elevated through 16:50.
payment-service errors are all 'ledger write failed: ... No space left on device', first at 15:00:26.
ledger-db emits 'No space left on device' PANIC/extend-file errors from 15:01 to 16:57.
ledger-db disk_used_pct grew from 84.03% at 12:00 to 100% at 15:02 and stayed at 100%.
ledger-db warned an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' was retaining up to 77 GB of WAL, first at 14:34 (before the deploy).
Only deploy in window: payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46, rolled back at 15:12; no config changes.
Errors continued well after the rollback (295 more from 15:20 to 16:57).
order-service, another ledger-db tenant, failed identically ('No space left on device') without any deploy.
ledger-db is shared by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service, settlement-service.
bank-partner-api error rate stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout.
Historical incident HIST-114 had the same root cause (inactive slot retaining WAL filling ledger-db disk).

assumptions: WAL retention warnings report the slot's retained bytes; the growth from 84% to 100% is dominated by retained WAL.
No unobserved process independently filled the ledger-db volume.
ledger-db telemetry (disk_used_pct) accurately reflects the data volume referenced in the 'No space left on device' errors.

timeline.event: ledger-db disk already at 84% and climbing steadily; no incident yet.
ledger-db warns replication slot 'analytics_cdc' inactive, retaining 33 GB WAL.
payment-service v6.0.0 deployed (New UPI mandate flow).
First payment-service ledger write failure (No space left on device); order-service also begins failing at 15:00:42.
ledger-db PANIC: cannot write WAL file, No space left on device.
ledger-db disk reaches 100% and stays there.
Errors continue (295 more through 16:57) despite rollback; disk still 100%.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately free disk on ledger-db: drop/advance the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' and, if needed, remove retained WAL to restore writes.
recommended_actions.rationale: The slot is holding tens of GB of WAL and disk is at 100%; clearing it is the direct fix. Same resolution as HIST-114.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating this as a bad deploy; do not continue rolling back unrelated services. The v6.0.0 rollback will not help.
recommended_actions.rationale: Errors persisted after the 15:12 rollback and a co-tenant failed without any deploy.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on replication-slot lag / inactive slots and on ledger-db disk_used_pct (warn >=85%, page >=95%).
recommended_actions.rationale: Disk grew from 84% to 100% over ~3 hours with no actionable alert; warn only at 98%.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate why the analytics_cdc consumer stopped advancing and add consumer-liveness monitoring.
recommended_actions.rationale: Root trigger is the consumer going inactive; preventing recurrence requires fixing the consumer.

recommended_actions.action: Add capacity planning / WAL-size guardrails on the shared ledger-db volume and review co-tenancy blast radius.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single shared Postgres disk exhaustion took down multiple payment-critical services simultaneously.

data_gaps: No metric directly attributes disk growth to WAL vs data; the WAL-retention warnings (33-77 GB) strongly suggest WAL, but the slot's exact retained size vs total volume isn't given.
ledger-db has no memory_pct / iops metric exposed (query for memory_pct returned not_found); disk I/O and inode metrics unavailable.
No telemetry for bank-partner-api (has_telemetry=false) — ruled out only via payment-service's flat bank_api_error_rate, not direct provider logs.
portfolio-service logs were not sampled; its failure status on ledger-db is inferred from shared-dependency graph but not directly observed.
The exact identity/owner of the analytics_cdc consumer and why it went inactive is not visible in the provided data.

First payment-service error is 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' at 15:00:26; this same pattern accounts for all 354 errors in the window (first_match 15:00:26).

findings.statement: ledger-db is a shared Postgres used by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service (dependency graph).
bank-partner-api error rate stayed flat at ~0.2% throughout (13:00-16:45), so the external dependency was healthy.
A prior incident HIST-114 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL' (2025-04-18) had the same root cause: inactive replication slot retaining WAL until disk filled.

refs.quote: Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled

findings.statement: Interpretation: payment-service errors are a downstream symptom of the ledger-db disk-exhaustion; the v6.0.0 deploy is temporally coincidental, not causal.
